description: Refines the noncanonical uniqueness of finite fields to the full Galois picture. The automorphism group Aut(GF(p^n)) over the prime subfield ZMod p is cyclic of order n, generated by the Frobenius x ↦ x^p (Subgroup.zpowers Frobenius = ⊤). Consequently, for two finite fields K, K' of order p^n the set of ZMod p-algebra isomorphisms K ≃ₐ K' is a torsor under Aut(K'): the post-composition action σ • f = f.trans σ is free and transitive and the set is nonempty, so fixing one isomorphism identifies the set with the Galois group — there are exactly n isomorphisms. Mathlib supplies cyclicity and the order/finrank facts; the explicit GF(p^n) packaging and the torsor structure are assembled here.
title: The Frobenius–Galois Structure of Finite Fields: Cyclic Automorphism Group and the Isomorphism Torsor

overview.historicalContext: The Galois theory of finite fields, going back to Galois's own work on congruences and codified by E. H. Moore (1893) and Dedekind, gives the most rigid possible structure theory: for each prime power q = p^n there is exactly one field of order q, and its automorphism group over the prime subfield 𝔽_p is cyclic of order n, generated by the Frobenius endomorphism φ : x ↦ x^p. The Frobenius is the single most important map in positive characteristic — its fixed field of φ^d is precisely the subfield 𝔽_{p^d}, so the lattice of subfields of 𝔽_{p^n} mirrors the lattice of subgroups of the cyclic group ℤ/nℤ (the Galois correspondence for the cyclic extension 𝔽_{p^n}/𝔽_p). This entry refines the parent's noncanonical uniqueness statement — that two fields of equal order are isomorphic — into the quantitative Galois picture: not only is the isomorphism set nonempty, it is a torsor under the cyclic Galois group, so there are exactly n isomorphisms and they are permuted simply transitively by powers of Frobenius.
overview.problemStatement: Strengthen the noncanonical uniqueness of finite fields to a Galois-theoretic statement. Prove that the automorphism group Aut(GaloisField p n) over its prime subfield ZMod p is cyclic of order n, generated by the Frobenius automorphism x ↦ x^p (equivalently Subgroup.zpowers Frobenius = ⊤). Deduce the torsor structure: for two finite fields K, K' of order p^n, the set of ZMod p-algebra isomorphisms K ≃ₐ K' carries a free and transitive post-composition action of Aut(K'), is nonempty, and therefore has exactly n elements.
overview.proofStrategy: Cyclicity is read off Mathlib's instance IsCyclic Gal(L/K) for finite field extensions. The order is computed by IsGalois.card_aut_eq_finrank (|Aut| = finrank) together with GaloisField.finrank = n; the same count is established for an arbitrary order-p^n field by deriving its finrank from |K'| = p^n via injectivity of the exponential n ↦ p^n. The Frobenius is identified as x ↦ x^p by unfolding coe_frobeniusAlgEquivOfAlgebraic and using |ZMod p| = p, and its order is n by orderOf_frobeniusAlgEquivOfAlgebraic = finrank. The generation statement Subgroup.zpowers Frobenius = ⊤ follows because the cyclic subgroup it generates has order |⟨Frobenius⟩| = orderOf Frobenius = n = |Aut| (Subgroup.card_eq_iff_eq_top). For the torsor, the post-composition action σ • f = f.trans σ of Aut(K') on the isomorphism set is shown free (left cancellation using surjectivity of f) and transitive (the witness f.symm.trans g), and fixing a base isomorphism f₀ yields the explicit equivalence autEquivIso : Aut(K') ≃ (K ≃ₐ K'); the count card_algEquiv_eq = n is the cardinality of this equivalence composed with |Aut(K')| = n.
keyInsights: The automorphism group of GF(p^n) is not merely cyclic (a Mathlib instance) but cyclic with a CANONICAL generator: the Frobenius x ↦ x^p. The content frobenius_generates makes 'generated by Frobenius' precise as Subgroup.zpowers Frobenius = ⊤, which the abstract IsCyclic instance does not single out.

Order equals generation: because |⟨Frobenius⟩| = orderOf Frobenius = n = |Aut(GF(p^n))|, the cyclic subgroup generated by Frobenius already exhausts the group. This is the cleanest route to 'Frobenius generates', avoiding any direct manipulation of automorphisms.

The isomorphism set between two order-p^n fields is a TORSOR, not a group: it has no distinguished element, but Aut(K') acts on it freely and transitively by post-composition. Choosing any one isomorphism f₀ trivialises the torsor, giving the bijection Aut(K') ≃ (K ≃ₐ K') and the count n.

Freeness and transitivity are elementary once the action is set up: freeness is left cancellation (f is an equivalence, hence surjective) and transitivity uses the explicit difference f.symm.trans g. The torsor abstraction packages exactly the two facts needed to count isomorphisms.

The 'mathlib' badge is honest: cyclicity (IsCyclic instance), the order of Frobenius (orderOf_frobeniusAlgEquivOfAlgebraic) and the order of the group (card_aut_eq_finrank) are Mathlib's; the new content is the explicit GF(p^n) packaging (order n, Frobenius = x ↦ x^p, Frobenius generates ⊤) and the torsor structure on the isomorphism set, which Mathlib does not record as named results.

openQuestions.question: Formalize the Galois correspondence for GF(p^n)/𝔽_p concretely: the fixed field of the d-th power of Frobenius φ^d is exactly the subfield GF(p^d), so the subgroup lattice of the cyclic group ℤ/nℤ matches the divisor lattice of subfields {GF(p^d) : d ∣ n}.

crossReferences.description: The parent proves the noncanonical uniqueness of finite fields (two fields of equal order are isomorphic, but no count or structure on the isomorphism set). This entry refines it: the automorphism group is cyclic of order n generated by Frobenius, and the isomorphism set is a torsor under it with exactly n elements.
A sibling line studies the subfield lattice and counting of monic irreducibles over GF(p); both rest on the Frobenius-Galois structure of finite fields developed here.

conclusion.summary: The Galois structure of finite fields is formalized: the automorphism group Aut(GaloisField p n) over its prime subfield is cyclic (Mathlib instance) of order n (card_aut_eq, from card_aut_eq_finrank and GaloisField.finrank), and is generated by the Frobenius automorphism x ↦ x^p (frobenius_apply, orderOf_frobenius = n, and frobenius_generates: Subgroup.zpowers Frobenius = ⊤). The set of ZMod p-algebra isomorphisms between two finite fields of order p^n is shown to be a torsor under the cyclic Galois group — nonempty (nonempty_algEquiv), with a free (trans_left_cancel) and transitive (exists_trans_eq) post-composition action and an explicit trivialisation autEquivIso — hence has exactly n elements (card_algEquiv_eq). The instance |Aut(GF(8))| = 3 is recorded. 167 lines, 11 theorems, 1 definition, 0 axioms, 0 sorries.
conclusion.implications: Cyclicity, the order of the group, and the order of Frobenius are Mathlib's (hence the mathlib badge); the new content is the explicit GF(p^n) packaging — order n, the Frobenius identified as x ↦ x^p, and the statement that it generates the whole group — together with the torsor structure on the isomorphism set, which Mathlib does not record. This upgrades the parent's qualitative uniqueness to the quantitative Galois description and sets up the Galois correspondence between the subgroup lattice of ℤ/nℤ and the subfield lattice of GF(p^n).
openQuestions: Make the Galois correspondence explicit: the fixed field of Frobenius^d is GF(p^d), matching the divisor lattice of subfields to the subgroup lattice of the cyclic Galois group.
